Steps: (1) confirmed the pinned closing block on an Ethereum mainnet RPC (https://api.opensea.io is the fact source; chain read from a public Ethereum JSON-RPC endpoint) - eth_getBlockByNumber(0x18d5d68) returns hash 0x15d372cb13fb07ab862d1c7028c830e26a0263f43beb787a79f0244f21ff923c, matching the brief, timestamp 1790184983. (3) Paged https://api.opensea.io/api/v2/listings/collection/world-of-women-nft/all (limit 100, followed 'next' to exhaustion): 137 active listings, every one priced in ETH with 18 decimals. The minimum current price is 85000000000000000 wei (0.085 ETH); the next two are 87999999000000000 and 88000000000000000. The cheapest three from .../best agree with the cheapest three of the full set, so the enumeration is complete. Caveat for readers: https://api.opensea.io/api/v2/collections/world-of-women-nft/stats reports total.floor_price 0.07204672990000023 ETH at the same moment. That float corresponds to no active listing in the full set and cannot be expressed exactly in wei; it is the cached/aggregated stats figure, lagging or counting a listing no longer active. The brief's definition asks for the lowest active listing, so the enumerated listing set is used and the stats float is rejected. Members who quote the stats field would land on ~72046729900000230 wei; that difference is the discrepancy to expect, and the listing enumeration is the primary reading. No wei value is derived from a floating-point conversion: 85000000000000000 is the integer the listing itself carries.
